The most important part of homesteading is a maintenance schedule. Everything requires some amount of upkeep. Set aside time in your week to do a maintenance project, whether it's sharpening your tools or reorganizing a space. You're a maintenance project too, but you should take time for yourself each day.

The easiest to implement strategy is copy-canning. Make a list of Nonperishable foods you eat. Next time you go to the store, by twice as much as you need. When you use one, buy two more. When it goes on sale, buy more. Consume them First-In-First-Out. Do this until you have at least a six week supply of food in your house in non-perishable food.

I mostly eat meat and animal products, but my girlfriend eats a modified Standard American Diet. We can both survive on my storage of canned fish, canned chili, Spam, powdered milk, honey, and peanut butter. Unless you're allergic to flour, you should have some on hand in an airtight container because it's the most nutrient dense food you can store.

I also store quite a bit of water in my small apartment in plastic protein powder containers. The plastic is BPA free, but I still worry about leeching and contamination, so I rotate through them to water my balcony garden.

My balcony garden is nothing to write home about. It's a kumquat tree, some succulents, and a snake plant. This year I'm sprouting tomatoes. We'll see how they do. I've killed a lot of plants.
